To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a knowledge repository for software assets origins selection is feasible; 2) it is based on a set of decision scenarios, each including a set of decision criteria, and a set of decision alternatives; 3) the decision process is based on a decision tree; and 4) the knowledge repository is based on a knowledge representation language that includes a set of decision templates.

a) a repository of software assets origin decisions can be used as a knowledge base for supporting decision making processes; b) the knowledge base can be used to support decisions at three levels: i) to support the decision maker to take a decision in the current scenario, ii) to support the analysis of a decision scenario, and iii) to support the identification of a set of decision alternatives; c) the knowledge base must include the following information: i) the decision maker, ii) the decision

a) the knowledge repository should include the decision context (i.e. the problem, the decision, and the decision makers); the decision rationale (i.e. how the decision was made); the decision outcome; and the decision consequences (i.e. its impact on the software system); and b) the repository should be queried to support decision making in the context of a new decision case.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: what information should be stored, how to store it, and when to use it.

the following questions: (1) What kind of information is relevant for the decision support process? (2) How to store it within a knowledge repository? (3) How to use the stored data in the decision making process?

the following research questions: (i) how to represent and retrieve historical decision information in a knowledge repository?; (ii) how to exploit the knowledge repository for decision support?; and (iii) how to evaluate the effectiveness of the decision support framework?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the knowledge repository will be used to store and retrieve information about the following aspects: (i) the decision scenario, (ii) the decision maker(s), (iii) the decision context, (iv) the assets, (v) the decision process, (vi) the decision rationale and (vii) the decision outcome.

the knowledge repository will provide the decision support system with the following information: (1) a set of assets (in the sense of components, services, and other reusable artifacts), (2) a set of decisions, each one of them being related to a set of assets, and (3) a set of scenarios, each one of then being a combination of a set of assets and a set of decisions.
the repository is a knowledge base of design decisions and their rationale, that can be used to support the decision making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ORION project aims to develop an approach for supporting software architects and engineers in making well founded decisions in the context of component based software development, and that the knowledge repository is one of the core elements of the ORION framework, which is currently under development.

the decision support system we aim to develop will be able to provide a set of decision scenarios, each one of them consisting of a decision context, a set of decision alternatives, a set of evaluation criteria, and an evaluation method, which are all derived from the historical decision information stored in the repository.

we aim at developing a framework in which decision making process is supported by a repository of past decisions, and that this repository can be used to support the decision making process itself, as well as the design of the software system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when dealing with software assets origin selection, a repository of past decisions and related information is a key element to be exploited in order to support decision making.

, when dealing with software assets selection decisions, the historical data about previous decisions is of paramount importance, and should be kept in a knowledge repository, to be used for decision support.
a decision knowledge repository can be used to support decision making, and to enhance the quality, consistency, and effectiveness of the decision making process.
